mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where this trigger is met, or the effect reverses in a statistically significant manner (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes, or the effect is absent in periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for S&P 500 constituents and leads to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive average returns over the 60-day horizon in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not robust during periods of stable monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, signals a manufacturing slowdown that reduces corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during periods of strong consumer demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL (core inflation) by more than 0.2% signals a disinflationary tightening, which initially depresses growth expectations but ultimately supports equity valuations via lower discount rates, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases AND CPIAUCSL decreases > -0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when unemployment rises sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their respective 12-month averages signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo avg AND UNRATE > 12-mo avg in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered months, or the effect reverses during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) of at least 5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports broader equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change >= +5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 does not deliver positive 20-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of rising mortgage rates.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a macroeconomic slowdown, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during periods of strong technological earnings growth.
